shortDescription: Stacks up to 7 playable z-levels (3 up / 3 down) into ONE banded RimWorld Map joined by synthetic RegionLink wormholes, so hauling, needs, work and storage come free from vanilla. Four vanilla-matched per-level sizes (126/190/250/300) and level counts are bought from a fixed 192,000-cell budget. Per-colony climate bands make high levels genuinely alpine. Content on lower levels draws smaller once per level of drop, which is what makes a deep column read as depth.
body:
> **NOTE TO SELF:** running spec, not a changelog. §1-19 architecture; §20 compat; §21-28 bug records. Keep every ⚠ - each cost a run to learn.

# As above, So below II (V2)

> V1 is DELETED. ~72 files, ~20,800 LOC. No em-dashes anywhere in shipped text.

## Pitch
Up to seven z-levels in ONE RimWorld `Map`. Priorities: (1) visual clarity from above, (2) performance, (3) vanilla parity.

## Status
Visuality, QOL, altitude/weather, settings VERIFIED. **250 tier VERIFIED (#236); 190x5 VERIFIED (#237-#240).**
**✅ §24b VERIFIED (#240, with BM): rock renders at every level.**
**✅ §24c VERIFIED (#248, vanilla / no BM): mass interiors solid, no pinhole grid.**
**✅ §27 VERIFIED: below-snow now fades outward at rocky peaks.**
**🔧 §28 FIXED, UNVERIFIED: the mass fill was a full-cell opaque QUAD under a stylised atlas tile, squaring off the silhouette past its own black outline - once per level.** Behind a dev toggle (`AB2: toggle mass field fade`).
**🔧 §25 FIXED, UNVERIFIED** (fog-on-reload + doubled/inverted stairs, one `ABSkySync` bug). Ships with a repair sweep for damaged saves.
UNVERIFIED: §25, §28, depth shrink, camera anchor, §18 audit, reroll grid, VEE compat, GL roof fix.

**PUBLISHED-BUILD BUGS.** 1. Preview 190-only - **FIXED** (§6d-CLAMP). 2. Fog/rocks on reload - **FIXED** (§25). 3. GL rivers - **TABLED with a contradiction** (§22). 4. MO formations 4x overlapping - **FIXED** (§24a). 5. Rock visible only one level down - **FIXED + VERIFIED** (§24b). 6. Stairs invert and double on reload - **FIXED** (§25). 7. Rounded-corner holes through below mass, non-BM only - **FIXED + VERIFIED** (§24c). 8. Below-snow fade inverted at rocky peaks - **FIXED + VERIFIED** (§27). 9. Square fill past the mass outline, stacking per level - **FIXED** (§28).

---

# 1. ARCHITECTURE
One `Map`, size `(w, 1, bandCount * Slot)`. Bands stack along +z from the deepest basement, gutter between. `Slot = ceil((bandHeight + MinGutter)/64)*64`; **64-alignment of SLOT is load-bearing** (terrain shaders sample by world position).

**The one insight.** `Region.Neighbors` is *topological, not spatial*. Wormhole `RegionLink`s between one-cell `RegionType.Portal` ends conduct connectivity without merging rooms, temperature or vacuum, and `Reachability.CanReach` works unpatched. But reachability is not a path: 1.6's pathfinder is jobified and cannot traverse a synthetic link, hence segmented movement (§3).

**Hard 1.6 constraints.** Path grid is IJobParallelFor over EVERY cell, so total stacked cells is the runtime metric. No `PathFinder.FindPath`. `BlocksDiagonalMovement` trips on unwalkable cells.

**⚠ The stack is 2x to 7x anisotropic.** Anything vanilla normalises by BOTH dimensions is distorted - a bug class that cannot appear on a square map.

### ⚠ THE SLICING RULE, seven shapes
| Shape | Example | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| Anchor, a fraction of `Size.z` | river/lake centre; random/edge cell; VEE Crater jitter | remap the point |
| Field, a gradient on map centre | coastline (§6e); VEE LoneIsland and Crater | re-centre the sample coordinate |
| Noise space, a slice is not a short map | Map Preview (§6d); GL landform grids (§22) | generate at full height, then crop |
| Distance-to-extent, a margin off `Size` | `CloseToEdge`, no-build edge; river WIDTH | re-base onto the cell's band rect |
| **Aspect ratio, normalised by BOTH dims** | preview window and reroll grid (§6d) | lay out from the BAND, generate at the STACK |
| **Map-wide scalar** | snow melt (§7), temperature readout (§16), GL roof sweep | rewrite it per cell at the consumer |
| **Foreign absolute writes** (§22) | GL landform output lands in band 0, our carve overwrites it | ORDER, not arithmetic |

Still unaudited: Basin, Cavern, Chasm, Cliffs, Hollow, Valley (all `FalloffAtAngle`).
**`ABBandLocal.cs` is THE canonical FIELD rewrite** plus `BandLocalModule`, a `ModuleBase` wrapper for direct noise samplers.

# 2. LEVEL PLAN, budget 192,000 cells
**⚠ THE 64 CONSTRAINT IS ON *SLOT*, NOT BAND HEIGHT.** The original tiers were all 64k-2 - the tightest fit - and **that coincidence was mistaken for the requirement for months**.

| size | slot | gutter | cells/band | playable | max levels | total |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 126 | 128 | 2 | 16,128 | 98.4% | 7 (cap) | 112,896 |
| 190 | 192 | 2 | 36,480 | 99.0% | 5 | 182,400 ✅ |
| **250** | 256 | 6 | 64,000 | 97.7% | 3 | **192,000** ✅ |
| **300** | 320 | 20 | 96,000 | 93.8% | 2 | **192,000** |

250/300 are vanilla's Medium and Large exactly. **Budget is tuned:** 192,000 = `3 x 64,000` = `2 x 96,000`. Ladder 7/5/3/2; 350/382 not offered because a second level exceeds the whole budget.
**⚠ 200 IS THE ONE NUMBER TO AVOID** - just past the 192 boundary: slot 256, gutter 56, 21.9% wasted. **Waste is a SAWTOOTH.**
**⚠ A WIDE GUTTER IS A FEATURE** - "a spatial helper that reaches 22 rows will cross a 2-row gutter" is the root of §15a and §4.
**Old saves are safe** - `bandHeight` is scribed; `SlotFor` is generic. **`Size.x == bandHeight` is a repair tool.**
**⚠ THE PLAN PERSISTS BETWEEN COLONIES AND SILENTLY CONSTRAINS THE SIZE.** Levels must be reduced BEFORE a larger size is selectable. Read the PLAN line before believing any size test.
**⚠ Own the widget, do not patch the data.** Our radio buttons write `GameInitData.mapSize` directly - **the authoritative record of the choice.** **Adding a tier means growing the `InitialSize` postfix** (now +288f). **The chooser LATCHES global state, released in a `Finalizer`.**

# 3-5. MOVEMENT, ORDERING, DESCENT
**Cross-band movement** segmented at ONE interception; hops must strictly decrease. **Multi-hop UNTESTED IN PLAY.**
**Group ordering:** the drag line between bands runs through the GUTTER; the odd/even signature ("3 and 5 fail, 2 and 4 do not") is the proof - only ODD counts sample exactly 0.5.
**⚠ ONE DESCENT RULE: `TryResolveVisibleBelow`.** TEN systems share it. **NINE appearances of the single-step bug** - eight as `- Slot` arithmetic, **the ninth (§24b) as a TERRAIN-DEF GATE with no arithmetic in it at all**, invisible to the standing grep audit. **`TryResolveVisibleFrom` is THE gate.**
**⚠ AND THE GATE ANSWERS TWO QUESTIONS, NOT ONE** (§27): *which* level a cell shows, and *whether* it shows anything. A consumer that resolves the centre and then reads raw grids for the neighbours has silently answered only the first.

# 6. SKY-MASS PRESENTATION
Despeckle (walls dissolve only at 7+ open neighbours; at 6 it ate the outermost wall row off every meadow edge), central fog hole, five-terrain plateau palette, cliff faces, alpine pass.
**⚠ The mass tapers with altitude, so +3 may contain NO LAND AT ALL.** Quantified (#237): surface 12,723 plants / fertility 0.631; +1 248 / 0.069; +2 170 / 0.046; +3 **37 / 0.012**.
**⚠ THE SKY BAND'S OWN MASS IS `AB_MountainTop` TERRAIN AND NOTHING ELSE IDENTIFIES IT.** `ABSkyBandGen` writes it for `KindLedge` (no edifice, no roof) and `KindWall` (rock edifice + `RoofRockThick`). A `KindLedge` cell is indistinguishable by terrain from a DERIVED mountain top, which is why `ABSkySync` may now only create `AB_MountainTop`, never overwrite one (§25).
**Snow-holding, and it decides where snow fades:** `AB_OpenAir` and `AB_WallTop` set `holdSnowOrSand=false`; **`AB_MountainTop` and `AB_RoofSurface` do NOT and therefore hold snow.** A `KindWall` cell still stays bare because its rock edifice is Full fillage and `SnowGrid.CanHaveSnow` rejects it. So vanilla's own snow layer fades correctly on a sky band unaided - which is what proved §27 was ours.

# 6a. ⚠ THE BELOW VIEW IS MIRRORED PASSES, NOT ONE RENDERER
`SectionLayer_ABBelowV2` ports vanilla `SectionLayer_Terrain` **and nothing else**. Confirmed five times: Water (§6b), Snow (§6f), **mass sprites (§24b)**, **linked corner fillers (§24c)**, **snow's visibility kernel (§27)**.
**⚠ THE CONVERSE IS HANDLED.** A foreign `Thing.Print` postfix prints into OUR layer and is still correct, because the call is bracketed `SnapshotVertCounts()` -> `Print` -> `FinishNewVerts`, and **`FinishNewVerts` transforms by VERTEX RANGE**. Preserve that.
**⚠ THREE DIFFERENT THINGS ARE ALL CALLED "MASS", AND THEY ARE REPRESENTED DIFFERENTLY.** This distinction cost three failed fixes (§24b):
| what | representation | drawn by |
|---|---|---|
| undug GROUND mountain | a real rock **edifice**, but FOGGED so its sprite is never printed | cap, from one Slot up |
| SKY-band mass | `AB_MountainTop` **terrain**, NO edifice at all | cap, into that band's own mesh |
| mined-out floor | rock leave-**terrain** | `ABMinedRockLookup` |
**Any code that tests only `edificeGrid` misses sky mass entirely; any code that tests only terrain misses undug ground.**
**⚠ AND THE MASS FILL IS EMITTED FROM THREE PLACES, NOT ONE** (§28): the cap's own in-band pass, `EmitMassRepresentationAt`, and `PrintBelowTerrain`'s base quad via the `AB_MountainTop` -> host-rough-stone substitution. **Any change to how mass FILL looks has to land in all three or it half-fixes and stacks.** They now share `EmitFieldAt` / `MassFanCoverage`.
**⚠ THE CAP IS SINGLE-STEP.** `SectionLayer_ABMountainCap` derives from `-bands.Slot`, exactly one band down. Correct for a sky band's own tapering mass; the cost is that nothing else drew mass deeper than one slot until §24b.
**Ascent rule:** the dirty mirror stops at the first opaque floor, tested over the cell and its eight neighbours; the FIRST step stays unconditional *because* the cap is single-step.
**⚠ THE UNIT OF WASTE IS A SECTION REGENERATION, NOT A CELL.**
**⚠ VISIBILITY IS DECIDED ENTIRELY BY `ABBands.ShowsBelow(terrain)`, SO A TERRAIN SWAP IS A RENDERING BUG.** `AB_WallTop` and `AB_OpenAir` are see-through; `AB_MountainTop` and `AB_RoofSurface` are opaque. Anything that rewrites one into the other silently changes what the whole below stack draws - that is §25.
**⚠ A SMOOTHING KERNEL IS A SECOND CONSUMER OF THAT SAME RULE** (§27). Any mirrored pass that averages over neighbours - snow today, and any future AO / edge / blend pass - must apply `ShowsBelow` to every sample, not only to the cell it is colouring.

# 6b-6g. WATER, PREVIEW, COASTS, SNOW, SHRINK
**Water** is TWO-PASS SCREEN-SPACE; `SectionLayer_ABBelowWatergen` targets `SubcameraDefOf.WaterDepth.LayerId`. Rivers remap `GetRiverCenter` (not `Init`); `GetLakeCenter` needs the same or it undoes the first. Width clamped at the producer. **⚠ ALL THREE INERT UNDER GL** (§22).
**⚠ 6d-CLAMP, PUBLISHED BUG:** `Stacked()` ran the incoming size through `Clamp()`, which returns *the largest offered size ≤ input that fits*. Map Preview passes VANILLA's size (250 default), so `Clamp(250)` returned 190 **regardless of the player's pick**. **Fix: `PlannedSize`** - the chooser already wrote the answer to `GameInitData.mapSize`.
**⚠ MAP PREVIEW SHIPS IN TWO HALVES AND GL BUNDLES ONE.** With GL installed and Map Preview absent, `Active` is TRUE while window types are ABSENT. **Do not "simplify" `Active`.**
**6d-REROLL:** the window opened EMPTY - `elementSize.y = 403/126*896 = 2,866 px` -> `gridSize.y = 0` -> `DesiredCount = 0`.
**Coasts:** CENTRED wrong, not scaled wrong. NO SCALING. **⚠ "None override `GetNoiseValue`" is about VANILLA ONLY.**
**6f. Below-snow:** no mirror of `SectionLayer_Snow` existed; the layer that fixed that had **never run on a cold map** until #248, and its first exposure produced §27. Geometry is built ONCE and only colours are rewritten - **never `ClearSubMeshes(All)` here**, or the colour count stops matching the vertex count. Every cell must emit exactly nine colours including invisible ones, or all later cells shift onto the wrong vertices.
**Depth shrink (UNVERIFIED):** **⚠ the atlas trap** - past `ZoomRootSize` 18 humanlikes render from a cached atlas blit ignoring `PawnDrawParms.matrix`. **⚠ natural rock excluded BY DEF, not by link type**, because BM makes rock non-linked.
**⚠ PERSPECTIVE MODE WAS BUILT AND REMOVED. Do not re-add as polish.**

# 7-8a. CHARACTER, CAMERA
Ore `x(1+0.45*(depth-1))` scales `basementOreDensity` through our OWN `ABOreGen.ScatterOres`. **⚠ The snow line never worked, and the comment saying it did not need to was wrong.**
**The camera clamp and level-switch input share `ABGuard.Camera`**, both per-frame paths where an unthrottled `Log.Error` turns a cosmetic bug into a hang.
**New-game anchor:** only `StartedNewGame` runs after vanilla's own camera jump. ⚠ OPEN: `z=24` was EXACTLY `PodScatterMargin`.

# 9. GENERATION COST

## 9a. The profile stamps its own conditions
Prints `TILE`, `PLAN`, `SCOPING:`, two censuses. Has voided or explained EIGHT comparisons - **#248 and #254 were both voided by their own TILE line before a single pixel was examined.** **⚠ THE WATER REPORT DOES NOT AND SHOULD.**

## 9b. ⚠ "COST IS DESTRUCTION NOT GENERATION" - NO LONGER TRUE, AND THE FIX IS WHY
#188 was 16/84. #231 is 71/29. Rock suppression worked, so the carve got cheap and cost moved to generation. **A historical record of a fixed problem.**

## 9c-9f. Measured cost curve, seven tiles
| run | plan | tile | gensteps | carve | total | destroyed | suppressed |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| #231 | 7x126 | Flat TropSwamp | 3,836 | 1,580 | ~5.7 s | 4,575 | 1,627 |
| #236 | 3x250 | SmallHills | 5,001 | **7,118** | ~12.4 s | 15,611 | 7,272 |
| #237 | 5x190 | Mountainous | 4,529 | 2,201 | ~6.9 s | 7,497 | 85,304 |
| #238 | 5x190 | SmallHills | 3,389 | 4,718 | ~8.3 s | 16,100 | 11,175 |
| #239 | 5x190 | Mountainous Desert | 2,217 | 2,357 | **~4.7 s** | 7,906 | 76,702 |
| #248 | 5x190 | Flat Tundra | 2,108 | 3,282 | ~5.4 s | 12,103 | 5,689 |
| #254 | 5x190 | Flat Desert | 2,133 | 3,033 | ~5.2 s | 12,920 | 5,889 |

**⚠ FillRock is SUPERLINEAR in band size:** 190 -> 36,480 cells -> ~960-2,200 ms; 250 -> 64,000 cells -> 4,254 ms. **1.75x cells, 2.87x time**, exactly as the `ListerThings` linear-`List.Remove` mechanism predicts.
**⚠ HILLINESS DECIDES THE BILL.** #237 vs #238 is a clean control - same tier, plan and biome, only hilliness differs - and the mountainous map SUPPRESSES 85,304 rocks while the small-hills map DESTROYS 16,100. Suppression is the cheap path.
**⚠ AND HILLINESS ALSO DECIDES WHETHER A RENDERING TEST IS VALID AT ALL** (#248, #254). A Flat tile spawns no mass wide enough to have mask-15 interior cells; a warm tile seeds no snow (`SeedAltitudeSnow` 1.3 ms on Desert 28.5C vs 4.6 ms on Tundra). **Read the TILE line before reading the screenshot.**
**⚠ THE 250 TIER IS THE EXPENSIVE ONE** (~12.4 s vs ~4.7-8.3 s at 190). I recommended the 192,000 budget reasoning about PATHFINDING and did not predict generation time would double.

## 9g. ⚠ RE-RANKED ON EVIDENCE, AGAINST MY OWN EARLIER ADVICE
`GenStep_Plants` across seven tiles: **2,270 / 2,225 / 1,086 / 1,326 / 61.5 / 464 / 92.5 ms** - a **37x spread**, dominated by rainfall.
I made four successive wrong claims about this one number: *"84% is grown then erased"* (false), *"biome-independent"* (dead at n=3), *"tracks hilliness"* (dead at n=4), *"1.1-2.3 s"* (dead at n=5).
**Basement `FillRock` is 960-4,254 ms on EVERY tile.** Tile-independent beats tile-dependent, so:
1. **Basement rock suppression** - consistently ~1.0-4.3 s. **Item 1.**
2. **`GenStep_Plants` traversal scoping** - 0.06-2.3 s. **Demoted.**
3. **`GenStep_RockChunks`** - `Filth_RubbleRock` is the top destroyed def on all seven tiles.
4. Scattered ruins (also a CONTENT BUG). 5. Perlin precompute (changes determinism).

# 10-12. PERF AND DIAGNOSTICS
59.6 fps at 96 pawns. **⚠ THAT BENCHMARK MEASURES THE WRONG THING** - cost is in section-regeneration BURSTS.
**⚠ Bisect toggles PERSIST across runs.** Now STAMPED INTO THE PROFILE.
**⚠ The pre-pinned palette always strips its LAST entry. n=8.** Keep padding with a DISTINCT throwaway.
**⚠ THE AUTO-PROMPT IS EDGE-TRIGGERED, SO CHECK THE COUNT, NOT THE TEXT.** `monitor_get_error` returns the LATEST occurrence, which may be the FIRST - byte-identical and stale.
**⚠ OUR OWN PROFILE ARRIVES AS A `warning` ROW ATTRIBUTED TO US.** It is deliberate (info level is filtered out of the bridge), so a run that reports "1 new error class" and nothing else is a CLEAN run. Read it for TILE/PLAN before concluding anything about the test.
**⚠ Debug actions are `AllowedGameStates.PlayingOnMap`** - silently inert on the world map / preview screen.
**⚠ AUDIT A DIAGNOSTIC'S OWN FILTERS BEFORE TRUSTING A NEGATIVE.** The below-layer report filtered on `StartsWith("SectionLayer_ABBelow")`, which excluded `SectionLayer_ABMountainCap`. **A missing row and an empty row are indistinguishable.** Now `SectionLayer_AB`.

# 13. OPEN WORK
1. **VERIFY §28** (A/B with `AB2: toggle mass field fade` on a mountainous map, several levels deep) and **§25** on the reporter's save.
2. **Basement rock suppression** (§9g item 1).
3. Verify tiers 126/300; preview at 300; §18 audit; VEE compat; GL roof fix; reroll grid; depth shrink; camera anchor.
4. Stamp TILE/PLAN into the water report.
5. §9g items 2-5; audit the other `FalloffAtAngle` mutators.
6. **Never exercised:** multi-hop stair router, elevator, basement PATHING/wormholes, cavern basement.
7. `ShotReport` drops target size. Biomes! at 40%. Better Trees unexamined (§23c). **Store page still says three levels.**
8. **§22 TABLED** - do not resume without re-reading the contradiction.
9. **CAI 5000 fog of war is a standing save-corruption risk we do not control** (§26). Only pursue if fog persists after §25.

# 14. LESSONS
**Method.** Prove a subsystem innocent by finding a state where the suspect CANNOT EXIST. Re-open a rejection only by naming the confound. Change one thing per experiment. Run the diagnostic before the third theory. A beautiful fit is not evidence.
**⚠ COUNT THE EMITTERS BEFORE FIXING THE LOOK.** §28's fill came from THREE places and the first two fixes would each have looked like a partial success - the artifact simply persisting on the levels the third owned. **When a symptom is "this appears once per level", the emitter count is the first thing to establish, not the last.** §6a now names all three.
**⚠ CLEAR THE OTHER SUSPECT BY READING ITS DATA, NOT ITS CODE.** §27 was "vanilla's snow layer or our mirror?" One grep of our terrain defs settled it: `holdSnowOrSand=false` on the see-through terrains plus Full fillage on `KindWall` rock means vanilla's kernel already sees zeroes in the right cells. **A def field can exonerate a whole layer faster than reading either layer.**
**⚠ A FIX FOR MOD X CAN BE A REGRESSION FOR EVERYONE WITHOUT X, AND THE BRANCH IS WHERE TO LOOK.** §24c: the BM fix added ONE emitter with two halves, and only the BM half was exercised in play. **When a fix lands as `if (foreignShape) A else B`, the untested branch is B, on the majority configuration.**
**⚠ REPRODUCING A SUBSYSTEM MEANS REPRODUCING ALL OF IT, NOT ITS MAIN OUTPUT.** An atlas tile is HALF of `Graphic_LinkedCornerFiller` (§24c). And the tile is only half of *vanilla rock*: **its TRANSPARENCY is load-bearing too** (§28). Anything opaque underneath fills the silhouette back in.
**⚠ A COMMENT THAT JUSTIFIES SKIPPING ONE CHECK CAN BE HIDING A SECOND CHECK IT NEVER MENTIONS.** §27's kernel carried a well-argued paragraph on why it does not re-resolve the DESCENT per neighbour - correct, and it quietly stood in for the missing VISIBILITY test. **When a comment defends an omission, name every question the omitted call would have answered.**
**⚠ AN EVENT HOOK THAT LOOKS INCREMENTAL MAY BE A FULL-MAP SWEEP ON THE LOAD PATH.** `Building.SpawnSetup` calls `edificeGrid.Register` **without consulting `respawningAfterLoad`** (§25). **Before trusting "this only fires on change", ask what the LOAD path does.**
**⚠ TWO RESOLVERS FOR ONE QUANTITY IS A BUG WITH A DELAY FUSE.** `ABSkyBandGen` and `ABSkySync` both answer "what terrain belongs above this cell" and disagreed on one rule. **When you add a live updater beside a generator, make one call the other or diff them line by line.**
**⚠ A FIX APPLIED TO ONE CASE MUST BE CARRIED TO ITS SIBLING CASE, AND THE COMMENT PROVES IT WAS NOT.** `ABSkySync`'s header documented "ROOF BEATS EDIFICE" and only the CONSTRUCTED-roof branch was ordered that way. **A confidently-written comment about a rule is where to look for the half that is missing.**
**⚠ READ THE GUARD CLAUSES OF THE HELPER YOU ARE ABOUT TO REUSE - INCLUDING YOUR OWN.** §24b attempt 1 routed through `EmitMassSilhouetteAt` after reading only its SIGNATURE; its body opens with three early returns.
**⚠ ASK HOW THE SUBSYSTEM REPRESENTS THE THING, NOT WHAT THE THING IS.** §24b attempt 2 assumed "mass" always means a rock edifice.
**⚠ THE USER'S REPHRASING IS DATA.** "lower level textures disappear" and "+2 does not show the rock ledge of +1" describe the same screen but different mechanisms.
**⚠ A DIRECTIONAL WORD IN A REPORT IS A GRADIENT, AND GRADIENTS COME FROM KERNELS.** "fades INWARD instead of OUTWARD" is not a colour or material bug; it says a weighted average is being fed the wrong samples. **Go straight to whatever averages over neighbours.**
**⚠ TWO SYMPTOMS REPORTED IN ONE BREATH ARE PROBABLY ONE BUG.** "Fog returns on reload" and "stairs invert and double" were the SAME line, both downstream of `ShowsBelow(terrain)`. **Ask what single quantity both symptoms read.**
**⚠ A SCREENSHOT CARRIES TERRAIN IDENTITY IF YOU KNOW YOUR OWN DEFS.** The grey tiled floor is `AB_RoofSurface`; the dark 2x2 behind the stairs is `AirMaskMat`. §24c: **shrunken sprites are a DEPTH READOUT** (the small tree said drop/slot = 2, picking the fogged emitter out of three candidates). §27: **hard, cell-aligned rectangles at a light/dark boundary mean a per-cell alpha written without its neighbours' agreement** - vanilla layers never produce a square edge, because every one of them smooths over a nine-vertex fan. §28: **a square that survives past a stylised outline is an opaque fill under transparent art**, and if it repeats per level, count the emitters.
**⚠ CHECK THAT YOUR CONFIGURATION CAN EXPRESS THE DIFFERENCE BEFORE RUNNING THE EXPERIMENT.** #231's water report was clean and worthless as a discriminator; #248's Flat tile and #254's warm Flat tile were the same mistake in map form.
**⚠ A CENSUS BEATS A MAGNITUDE - AND I IGNORED MY OWN RULE.**
**⚠ n=2 IS NOT A PATTERN, AND NEITHER IS n=4.** On a multi-factor quantity, report the RANGE and stop naming drivers.
**⚠ TILE-INDEPENDENT WINS BEAT TILE-DEPENDENT ONES.** Rank by worst case across conditions.
**⚠ Measure the ratio before optimising the half you assumed - and RE-measure after.**
**⚠ A FIX CAN BE CHEAPER THAN THE BUG.** §27 replaced 289 gate calls + 8-per-visible-cell raw reads with 361 cached ones over a one-cell apron. **When a per-cell test has to become a per-neighbour test, cache the apron rather than accepting the 9x.**
**⚠ WHEN A NEW RULE IS THE DUAL OF AN EXISTING ONE, SAY SO IN THE CODE.** `ABNineFan.Cover` is a dilation, `CoverInterior` an erosion; they have identical signatures and swapping them compiles and looks *almost* right (scalloped edges instead of retracted ones). **Near-miss failure modes need the near-miss documented, not just the rule.**
**⚠ THE SYMPTOM SET IS ITSELF EVIDENCE.** §21 named fog AND rocks and nothing else, and I read that as "flat per-cell arrays sized by `map.Area`" - perfect fit, wrong. **A symptom pair narrows the search; it does not pick between two mechanisms that both explain it.**
**⚠ A LOSSY NORMALISER IS NOT A WAY TO READ A CHOICE.** **⚠ A CONSTRAINT SATISFIED BY EVERY EXAMPLE IS NOT NECESSARILY THE CONSTRAINT.** **⚠ A RULE ENFORCED BY GREPPING A SYNTAX ONLY CATCHES THAT SYNTAX.** **⚠ A DESIGN CHOICE RECORDED WITHOUT ITS COST WILL BE READ AS FREE.** **⚠ THE REAL CONFLICT IS USUALLY A REPLACEMENT, NOT A COLLISION.** **⚠ AND THE BUG AFTER THAT IS USUALLY A COLLABORATION** - when neither side is wrong, look at the ORDER.
**⚠ CHECK WHETHER IT IS ALREADY BUILT BEFORE BUILDING IT.** §24c arrived as "we need a soft reflection check for BM" - the branch already existed and was type-based. **The requested mechanism is a hypothesis about the cause, not the cause.**
**⚠ A SHARED METHOD NAME IS A HYPOTHESIS, NOT A CONFLICT.** False-positive rate 50%; ReGrowth cleared four times.
**⚠ Compat work is mostly deletion.** **⚠ Design for the foreign patch you have not met.** **⚠ Waste is often a sawtooth.** **⚠ The thing you rounded away may be load-bearing.** **⚠ Duplication is how an invariant dies.** **⚠ A comment is not an invariant.** **⚠ Steady-state fps hides burst cost.** **⚠ Timing that reads exactly 0.0 ms is an early return.** **⚠ In a foreign log, the loudest error is usually downstream.** **⚠ A finding scoped to vanilla does not transfer to mods.**
**Patching.** Re-aim the shared parameter. Find the ONE virtual everything funnels through - and when there is none, **wrap the DATA instead of the reader**. Patch the PRODUCER, not the store. Own the widget. Never put a foreign type in a patch signature - type `__instance` as `object`. **Suppress the callee, not the caller.** **Prefix state is released in a Finalizer.** **Repair a foreign method's output rather than reimplementing it.** **Never clamp a Def field to fix one map.** **Prefer a published ExtensionPoint over racing internals.** **Read the LIVE def field, never a baked copy, when a mod can rewrite it at runtime.** **When a helper returns bool, use its return as the hand-off signal rather than duplicating its guards** (§24b).

Draw order is material render QUEUE, not altitude. `Banded` is FALSE for all of map generation. `SectionLayer` subclasses auto-discovered on EVERY map. Ore defs have no `naturalTerrain` **and no `_Rough` terrain at all**. `CameraJumper.TryJump` and `MapDrawer.MapMeshDirty` return silently unless `ProgramState == Playing`. ## 24a. FIXED: MO formations drawn four times overlapping
`IsPrintAnchor` picks the first cell of a multi-cell thing whose viewing cell can see it - single-valued **only if every cell resolves to the same `drop`**. It does not. Fixed by deduping per THING per Regenerate pass. **Never MO-specific.**

## 24b. ✅ FIXED AND VERIFIED (#240): rock renders at every level
The cap derives from one Slot down; the below layer's bridge fired only for `def == AB_MountainTop`; and every cross-level path ran through `EmitMassSilhouetteAt`, which returns false for mineable edifices and non-linked graphics. `EmitMassRepresentationAt` draws the mass itself, reached via the silhouette's own bool return and from the `foggedBelow` branch gated `drop > slot`.

## 24c. ✅ FIXED AND VERIFIED (#248): rounded corners read as holes, non-BM only
Vanilla rock fell into the ATLAS half, which drew `SubMaterialFromAtlas(mask)` and nothing else - half of vanilla's drawer. Fix: corner fillers on the exact vanilla rule; mask 15 skipped when the field was drawn; `MassLinked` with off-map counting as LINKED; field falls back to host stone's rough terrain (**ore has no `naturalTerrain`**).

## 24d / §28. 🔧 FIXED (UNVERIFIED): THE FILL SQUARED OFF THE SILHOUETTE, ONCE PER LEVEL
**Report, from a night shot of a multi-level mountain:** "every layer creates a new layer on top. At the mountain edges we get both the stylized black border of mineable rock, and the square texture."

**Root cause.** Vanilla rock is ONLY its atlas tile, and that tile's TRANSPARENCY is load-bearing - the rounded corners and wavy lip are the silhouette. We draw an opaque full-cell fill underneath it, which fills those gaps back in, so past the black border the cell squares off. Every level draws its own fill, so it compounds downward exactly as reported.

**⚠ THREE EMITTERS, NOT ONE** - and fixing any one alone would have looked like a partial success:
1. `SectionLayer_ABMountainCap.Regenerate` - the cap's own in-band field quad;
2. `EmitMassRepresentationAt` - the cross-level field quad (§24b/§24c);
3. `SectionLayer_ABBelowV2.PrintBelowTerrain` - the BASE terrain quad, which is where a sky-band mass gets its rock when viewed from above, via the `AB_MountainTop` -> host rough stone substitution.

**Fix: erode the fill to the same link rule the tile's mask uses**, via `ABNineFan.CoverInterior` - the DUAL of `Cover`. `Cover` is a dilation (union: any matching neighbour claims its points, a border growing inward from outside); `CoverInterior` is an erosion (intersection: a perimeter point survives only if everything touching it continues; centre always survives). An all-linked cell yields a fully covered fan, geometrically the same square the quad drew, **so mass interiors are byte-identical and §24c's verified look is untouched**.
- Sites 1 and 2 share `EmitFieldAt`; site 3 uses `MassFanCoverage`. Each caller passes its OWN link rule's answers, because they legitimately differ: the cap counts MEADOW as linked (its fill must not retract at a plateau boundary, where the meadow fans own the transition and no lip is drawn), the cross-level emitter counts only mass.
- Link tests are hoisted above the fill at both sites, since mask and fill now read one set of answers.
- `FieldFadeClone` is kept separate from `FieldClone` so the cap's opaque quads cannot change shader as a side effect. Generated stone is already `FadeRough`, so no swap fires on vanilla rock; the `TerrainHard` -> `TerrainFadeRough` swap is defensive, for modded rock whose rough terrain is Hard-edged (a Hard shader ignores vertex alpha, and the fan would silently render as a full square).
- `ABNineFan.AddFan` now has a per-vertex-colour core so the cliff-face ramp survives the fan's THREE vertex rows (a fan has mid-edge and centre verts at z+0.5 that a quad does not).
- Dev A/B: **`AB2: toggle mass field fade`**, flipping all three at once deliberately.

# 25. 🔧 FIXED (UNVERIFIED IN PLAY): ONE `ABSkySync` BUG, TWO PUBLISHED SYMPTOMS
**The trigger, shared.** `Building.SpawnSetup` calls `map.edificeGrid.Register(this)` **without consulting `respawningAfterLoad`**. `Map.FinalizeLoading` respawns every building including every compressed `Mineable`, so `ABSkySync.SyncAbove` re-derives the ENTIRE sky band on every load. Both symptoms are reload-only and both compound, because the rewritten terrain is then saved.

**(a) The fog blob - `AB_MountainTop` -> `AB_WallTop`.** `Resolve` tested *impassable edifice* before *natural roof*. Undug rock is an impassable edifice under a natural roof, so every cell above unmined surface rock resolved to `AB_WallTop`, which is `dontRender` and `ShowsBelow`-true: the mass turned see-through and `EmitBelowFogFan` painted the SURFACE's fog through it.

**(b) The doubled, inverted stairs - `AB_RoofSurface` -> `AB_OpenAir`.** `CarveLanding` writes the landing *after* `base.SpawnSetup` already ran the sync. `Resolve` sees an unroofed `Building_Door` (`PassThroughOnly`) and returns `AB_OpenAir`; the landing goes see-through and the level below's stairwell prints into it. Up-art and down-art are vertical mirrors.

**Fix, four parts.** (1) precedence is constructed roof -> **natural roof** -> impassable edifice -> open air; (2) `IsDerived` no longer contains `AB_MountainTop` - the rule is **one-way**; (3) `SyncAbove` bails on `CarriesOwnStructure` and on the solid -> air transition within a link's landing apron; (4) `RepairAfterLoad` from `ABBandMap.FinalizeInit`, **placed there because that is the first moment this load's damage has already happened**.
**⚠ THE REPAIR IS TWO NARROW TRANSITIONS, NOT A RE-DERIVE.** Both rules can only move a cell back to a state the generator itself produces. Idempotent; logs a count when it repairs anything.

# 27. ✅ FIXED AND VERIFIED: BELOW-SNOW FADED THE WRONG WAY AT ROCKY PEAKS
**Report (#248, first cold map to exercise §6f):** "snow on the upper level fades inward towards other snow covered tiles instead of outward toward the rocky peaks", plus hard cell-aligned rectangles where snow met rock.
**Not vanilla's layer** - see §6.
**Root cause.** The layer resolved see-below visibility for the CENTRE cell, then sampled the nine-neighbour kernel straight out of `SnowGrid` at `z - drop`. A neighbour under a rocky peak is opaque from above, but its *lower-level* cell usually has snow, so the kernel read off-screen snow and held full opacity right up to the peak; the opaque cell writes alpha 0 across its own nine vertices, giving the square edge. The only place alpha could ramp was the interior.
**Fix.** A one-cell-apron visibility cache built once per Regenerate from the shared gate, and three sample classes where there were two: outside the playable band -> **centre depth** (vanilla's map-edge rule, band-local, so no fade stripe grows along a band seam); inside the band but not visible -> **zero**; visible -> sample at the centre's drop. **361 gate calls over the apron instead of 289 plus eight per visible cell.**
